subject: Re: HealthScope — model fit & safety follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-23T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: HealthScope — follow-up and next steps (model fit & safety)

Hi Susan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

- Goal recap: you want an LLM assistant for clinician triage notes (summarization + assistant), with strict refusal behavior for sensitive mental-health and self-harm prompts, and an audit trail for every inference.
- Recommended immediate evaluation plan: run 1) model fit benchmarks on your de-identified triage corpus, 2) safety/refusal evals using our sensitive prompt suite, 3) latency/cost profiling for peak-hour estimates.

Deliverables we committed to: 
1) Suggested model set (fast experiments): redwood-7b-qat, redwood-13b-fp16, redwood-70b-llm, plus a distilled safety-tuned variant for refusals. 
2) Prompt set + example golden outputs (attached: healthscope_prompt_set_v1.txt).
3) Safety evaluation summary and a link to the eval dashboard (link below).
4) A short mutual action plan and POC timeline (we can align on this once you confirm dataset availability).

Notes on safety/guardrails based on our discussion: 
- We observed higher false-accept rates for open-domain self-harm prompts on larger instruction-tuned models in internal tests; our safety-tuned variants add refusal-class fine-tuning and hard-coded guard checks (prefix-based triggers) to reduce those.
- For auditability, we can enable token-level logging and per-request metadata (request_id, model_version, filter_flags) in Redwood Private or Dedicated.

Next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm which de-identified sample (1k records) we can ingest and share a secure link (SFTP or Drive).
- Us: run the model-fit and safety evals within 5 business days after sample receipt and share results + suggested model/quantization profile.
- Schedule 30-min follow-up to review results (I proposed Tue 6/30; Vivek will share calendar options).

I attached the initial prompt set and will push a curated safety-eval summary to the dashboard once runs complete. Anything I missed?

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) On the safety side, our compliance team is specifically worried about minimization of false negatives for self-harm and controlled-substance advice. Can you share the threshold metrics you use for "false-accept" and what remediation you recommend if a model fails?
2) For data transfer: we can provide a de-identified S3 bucket (read-only for your eval account). I'll confirm with security and share the link by EOD Monday.

Tom and I are also curious about cost tradeoffs between the 13B quantized option and the 70B model for production — if you can include rough token-cost estimates in the eval report that would help.

—Susan
Head of Clinical Ops, HealthScope

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@healthscope.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthScope — follow-up and next steps (model fit & safety)

Hi Susan — great questions, answered inline below. Looping in Neha from our security/compliance team to provide any SOC/PII notes if needed.

1) False-accept thresholds and remediation:
- We report precision/recall for the refusal class on the safety suite. For triage/self-harm we recommend tuning for recall >= 0.95 on the refusal class (i.e., minimize false negatives), with precision target >= 0.80 to avoid excessive unnecessary refusals. If a model fails the recall target, remediation options include: 1) safety fine-tuning on refusal-labeled examples, 2) combining model-based refusal with deterministic rule-based filters (regex/keyword and context windows), 3) adjusting the decision threshold on the refusal classifier head. We'll include per-model metrics and recommended remediation steps in the runbook.

2) Cost/latency: we'll produce per-token cost estimates for the quantized 13B vs 70B (real numbers in the report). Rough ballpark: with QAT quantization the 13B can be ~3-4x cheaper per token and meet sub-200ms p50 for our batching profile for short clinical prompts; the 70B gives higher fidelity on edge cases but is ~6-8x the cost and higher tail latency. Exact numbers will be in the eval dashboard.

Attached is a short safety-eval summary (preliminary) and the prompt set you requested. Once we get the S3 link we'll kick off the runs and post results to the dashboard here: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/HS-2026-0421

Do you want Neha or Vivek to join Tuesday's follow-up to go over technical remediation details?

Thanks — Marissa

Attachment: redwood_safety-eval-summary-20260623.pdf
